extracted.intended_audience: regulatory stakeholders, device/drug manufacturers, lawyers, policy researchers tracking FDA rules
extracted.subtask_description: An API/listing page aggregating recent Food and Drug Administration (FDA) rule documents (titles, abstracts, document numbers, urls, publication dates) describing device classifications, reclassifications, codifications, regulatory amendments, and related final rules. Useful for tracking FDA rulemaking actions and their stated requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification into class II (special controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is classifying [device] into class II (special controls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstracts state that the special controls that apply to the device type are identified in the order and will be part of the codified language for classification. The Agency states it determined that classifying the device into class II will provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness and may enhance patient access by reducing regulatory burdens. Examples in the listing include external condoms for anal/vaginal intercourse, circulating tumor cell enrichment devices, corneal storage media with preservatives, and many others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of special controls to provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is establishing the special controls necessary to provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness of these devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special controls are identified in the final order and will be codified in the device classification regulation. For reclassified devices, special controls often accompany the reclassification to class II and serve as the mitigation measures that, together with general controls, provide reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness. The listing repeatedly notes that those special controls will be part of the codified regulatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassification of devices (including from class III to class II) and codification under new regulation names
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is issuing final orders reclassifying certain postamendments class III device types into class II (special controls) and renaming/codifying them under new classification regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: optical diagnostic devices for melanoma detection and electrical impedance spectrometers are reclassified and renamed to 'software-aided adjunctive diagnostic devices for use on skin lesions by physicians trained in the diagnosis and management of skin cancer.' Reclassification actions include codification of the new classification regulation and establishment of associated special controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premarket notification requirement for reclassified devices
rubrics_metrics.description: When FDA reclassifies certain devices into class II, the reclassification may be 'subject to premarket notification.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listing explicitly states that reclassified devices (e.g., non-invasive bone growth stimulators) are being reclassified into class II, subject to premarket notification (510(k)). This indicates an evaluative/ procedural requirement tied to reclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of effective date following timely objections
rubrics_metrics.description: The delay of an effective date is required by law following the filing of timely objections on a final order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts for color additive final orders note that a filing of timely objections (and requests for hearing) triggers a statutory delay of effectiveness. The agency clarifies that such a delay does not change its underlying safety determination (e.g., 'reasonable certainty of no harm') nor does it itself determine that objections justify a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and exceptions for listing color additives exempt from certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations for safe use of color additives are limited to specified conditions and include enumerated exceptions (e.g., USDA-jurisdiction products, infant formula, foods with standards of identity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: beetroot red authorized for coloring human foods generally 'at levels consistent with current good manufacturing practice, except in products under the jurisdiction of the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA), infant formula, or foods for which standards of identity have been issued under section 401 of the FD&C Act, unless the use ... is authorized by such standards.' Other actions (e.g., spirulina extract) also lower heavy metal specifications and add a cadmium specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize National Drug Code (NDC) format and revise barcode requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All FDA-assigned NDCs will be required to be 12 digits in length with 3 distinct segments and 1 uniform format: 6-digit labeler code, 4-digit product code, and 2-digit package code; drug product barcode label requirements are revised to permit use of other data carriers that meet the standards of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule standardizes the NDC format to reduce ambiguity and revises barcode label requirements to allow other data carriers that comply with the new standards. This is a concrete formatting/labeling requirement described in the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend animal drug regulations to reflect application-related actions and improve accuracy/readability
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is amending the animal drug regulations to reflect application-related actions for NADAs, ANADAs, and CNADAs (e.g., approval, withdrawal, change of sponsor) and to improve the accuracy and readability of the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listing notes these amendments update regulatory text to reflect recent application-related actions (for specified months) and make non-substantive improvements to clarity and correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification and renaming of device types to reflect intended use and user population
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA renames and codifies device types under new classification regulation titles that reflect intended use and user qualifications (e.g., 'software-aided adjunctive diagnostic devices for use on skin lesions by physicians trained in the diagnosis and management of skin cancer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These renamings clarify the scope, intended user population, and regulatory expectations for the device type and accompany establishment of special controls appropriate to that scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stated policy rationale: balance safety/effectiveness assurance with enhancing patient access by reducing regulatory burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA repeatedly states that classifying devices into class II (with appropriate special controls) will provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness and may also enhance patient access to beneficial innovative devices by reducing regulatory burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy rationale appears across multiple classification/reclassification abstracts and serves as an explicit evaluative standard guiding when reclassification or application of special controls is appropriate.
